evidence.V2: Clear tiers: big (plinth / shaft / abacus), medium (torus base, echinus flare), small (thin gold necking band, chamfered abacus and plinth edges).
evidence.V3: Confidently stylised: oversized chunky abacus and plinth against a slimmer shaft give a cartoon-classical read; seating is correct (shaft on base and capital on shaft both seated).
evidence.V4: Close_capital and close_base studio show consistent chamfers on the abacus, plinth and torus that catch clean highlight lines.
evidence.V5: Close_shaft studio shows irregular wavy, smeared light/dark streaks running down the whole shaft while the flat close-up shows a straight, featureless outline: a shading artifact (wobbly normals / half-formed fluting) that reads as wood grain, especially in the sandstone and brick colourways.
evidence.V6: One stone hue in three values (dark plinth/abacus, mid torus, light shaft) plus a single gold accent band; colourways keep the structure.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, stone hue + gold band per wave-2 modular spec and kit chamfers, but the streaky shaft shading departs from the kit's clean smooth weighted-normal look and makes stone read as timber.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, MeshPart white + SmoothPlastic, grid-corner pivot; T1 vertical tiling passes (iou 1.0).

artifacts: Wavy smeared shading streaks along the entire shaft (close_shaft studio), not backed by visible geometry in the flat close-up
top_fixes: Fix the shaft shading: either model real, evenly spaced flutes with clean weighted normals or make the shaft a clean smooth cylinder
Optionally add slight entasis or a second gold/ink band at the base of the shaft to strengthen the small tier
Check the sandstone/brick colourways after the shading fix so the shaft reads as stone, not wood
